subject: humanities
passage: The Ajanta Caves, cut into a horseshoe-shaped cliff in western India, were carved and painted by Buddhist monks and artists between about the second century BCE and the fifth century CE. Their wall paintings show scenes from the lives of the Buddha alongside crowded palaces, markets, and forests. After the site was abandoned, it lay hidden by forest for centuries, until a British officer on a hunting trip came upon one of the caves in 1819. Today the paintings are valued not only as religious art but also as a rare record of everyday life, dress, and architecture in ancient India.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that the Ajanta paintings are the finest religious art ever produced in India
choices.B: To describe how a British officer came upon the caves while hunting in 1819
choices.C: To introduce the Ajanta Caves and explain why their paintings are valued today
choices.D: To explain why Buddhist monks abandoned the Ajanta Caves after the fifth century

explanation.why: The text tells when and by whom the caves were made, what the paintings show, how the site was rediscovered, and finally why the paintings matter: they are valued as religious art and as "a rare record of everyday life." A choice must cover this overview and its point about the paintings' value.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the paintings are valued, but it never ranks them against all other religious art in India.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The officer's discovery is one detail in the history of the site, not the purpose of the whole text.
explanation.C: Correct. The text presents the caves' history and contents and ends by explaining the two reasons the paintings are prized.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the site was abandoned but never gives a reason.
